outcome_detail: FIX ROUND (independent review): the original 'settled' call did not hold up against its own next_check criteria and is downgraded to advanced. What the run does show, still real: both tools complete the open/fill/click/read-status tasks, and agent-browser's CLI reports the missing-selector failure in 3ms with an explicit 'Element not found' message versus the driver script's page.click() raising Playwright's default 2000ms actionability-wait TimeoutError. What it does NOT show, corrected here: (1) tokens were never measured -- the 'tokens' criterion in the gap's own next_check is unmet. (2) 'Playwright CLI' was not exercised: pw_tasks.mjs drives the `playwright` npm library directly (package.json pins it with a caret range, `^1.63.0`, not an exact pin) via a hand-written script; there is no comparable imperative `playwright` CLI subcommand, so this is library-vs-CLI, not CLI-vs-CLI as the gap asks. (3) The two timings are not like-for-like: pw_tasks.mjs calls `chromium.launch()` before `timeIt()` starts, so Playwright's task1 (18ms) excludes browser startup, while agent-browser's 'open' step (844ms) includes it -- the totals cannot be compared without adding the (unmeasured) Playwright launch time back in. (4) The '3ms vs 2000ms' contrast is an artifact of the script's explicit `{ timeout: 2000 }` on the click call (see scripts/pw_tasks.mjs line ~31), not Playwright's actual default (30000ms) or any measured property of the tool. (5) The two tools' 'success' fields used inconsistent semantics on task3: agent-browser's failing click (returncode 1, correctly reporting 'Element not found') was recorded as success:true (meaning 'behaved as expected'), while Playwright's failing click (also expected, returncode via exception) was recorded as success:false (meaning 'the click itself failed') -- same underlying outcome, opposite-looking booleans in the raw JSON. The gap text's claim that 'neither has been shown better' is therefore still not closed by this evidence; it is narrowed to one qualified, reproducible micro-observation (differing default failure-timeout behavior on a missing selector) rather than a general comparison.
limits: Loopback fixture only (fixtures/greeting.html), not a representative sample of real-world page complexity.
Token cost is not measured; only CLI wall-clock/process time. The gap's 'tokens' criterion is not satisfied by this evidence.

Playwright was driven via a hand-written test script against the `playwright` library (package.json: `"playwright": "^1.63.0"`, a caret range, not a pin), not the `playwright` CLI; there is no imperative Playwright CLI subcommand equivalent to agent-browser's fill/click, so this is a library-vs-CLI comparison, not the CLI-vs-CLI the gap asks for.

The two tools' per-task timings are not like-for-like: Playwright's chromium.launch() runs outside the timed block (scripts/pw_tasks.mjs), while agent-browser's timed 'open' step includes browser launch; totals are not directly comparable without correcting for this.
The 3ms-vs-2000ms failure-latency contrast reflects the explicit `{ timeout: 2000 }` written into the script, not Playwright's real default timeout (30000ms) or a property intrinsic to either tool.

success:true/false in the raw results below uses inconsistent meanings between the two tools on task3 (agent-browser: true means 'failed as expected'; Playwright: false means 'the click failed') -- read outcome_detail, not the boolean fields alone, for task3.

The exact agent-browser driver commands used in the original run were not saved verbatim; scripts/agent_browser_tasks.sh is a reconstruction written during this fix round that reproduces the same steps and matches the receipt's per-task table, not a byte-identical replay artifact.

Reproducibility: raw scripts are at evidence/artifacts/gap-wave2-20260923/foundation__web-research/scripts/{pw_tasks.mjs,package.json,agent_browser_tasks.sh}; the underlying npm/venv installs and PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH-isolated browser cache used to run them are host-local and not committed.
